description: The metric panel for a predictive-superiority claim, and what each one can be gamed by. The panel is reported whole: ranking on a single metric is how a model wins by sacrificing everything the metric does not see.

metrics.label: Perturbation Discrimination Score
metrics.gameable_by: embedding structure alone, with no accurate magnitudes

metrics.label: Differential Expression Score
metrics.gameable_by: predicting the globally most frequently differential genes

metrics.label: Mean absolute error
metrics.gameable_by: predicting nothing changed — dilution toward the control mean

metrics.label: Pearson on control-referenced change
metrics.gameable_by: little, which is why it is in the gate set

metrics.label: Absolute-expression Pearson
metrics.gameable_by: the absolute-expression scale artifact — reported to expose it, never ranked on

baselines.why: if this wins, the model has not learned the perturbation

baselines.description: mean of the training perturbation profiles
baselines.why: catches a model that has learned only the average response

baselines.description: control plus the average training delta
for a double A+B: single_A + single_B - control
baselines.why: mandatory for combination claims, and hard to beat

rules: The model must beat the strongest baseline on EVERY gate metric, by a stated margin. Beating on average is not beating.
Thresholds are prespecified and enforced simultaneously, so one metric cannot be traded for another.
If a model's rank moves by two or more places across the gate metrics, the panel is unstable and the report must show it rather than picking the flattering ordering.
A distance metric is only admissible if it has been shown to behave in the dimensionality it is used at. Report the panel, not a composite.
